endpoint.text: Primary endpoint: progression-free survival (PFS); key secondary endpoint OS.

citations.quote: The pre-specified analyses of PFS and OS in SPOTLIGHT were determined to be statistically significant.
A total of 565 patients were randomized, 283 to the zolbetuximab.clzb arm and 282 to the placebo arm.

result.text: PFS HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.598, 0.942; 1-sided p=0.0066), median PFS 10.6 vs 8.7 months; OS HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.601, 0.936; 1-sided p=0.0053), median OS 18.2 vs 15.5 months.

citations.quote: The PFS hazard ratio (HR) was 0.75 (95% CI: 0.598, 0.942; 1-sided p=0.0066) with a median PFS of 10.6 months (95% CI 8.9, 12.5) in the zolbetuximab.clzb and chemotherapy arm vs. 8.7 months (95% CI 8.2, 10.3) in the placebo and chemotherapy arm.

The OS HR was 0.75 (95% CI: 0.601, 0.936; 1-sided p=0.0053) with a median OS of 18.2 months (95% CI: 16.4, 22.9) in the zolbetuximab.clzb and chemotherapy arm and 15.5 months (95% CI: 13.5, 16.5) for the placebo and chemotherapy arm.

target_moa.text: Chimeric (mouse/human) IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds claudin-18 isoform 2 (CLDN18.2) and depletes CLDN18.2-positive cells via ADCC and CDC.

citations.quote: Zolbetuximab.clzb is a chimeric (mouse/human) monoclonal antibody that binds claudin-18 isoform 2 (CLDN18.2).
Zolbetuximab.clzb is a cytolytic antibody that depletes CLDN18.2-positive cells via antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) and complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC).

Zolbetuximab.clzb is a chimeric (mouse/human) antibody composed of variable regions derived from mouse anti-human claudin-18 isoform 2 monoclonal antibody and constant regions derived from human IgG1.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥15%): nausea, vomiting, fatigue, decreased appetite, diarrhea, peripheral sensory neuropathy, abdominal pain, constipation, decreased weight, hypersensitivity reactions, pyrexia. More nausea (76%) and vomiting (67%) with zolbetuximab-clzb vs placebo (56% nausea, 33% vomiting). Serious adverse reactions in 45% of SPOTLIGHT patients; discontinuation due to AE in 20%.

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions (\ge 15\%) for VYLOY in combination with mFOLFOX6 or CAPOX were nausea, vomiting, fatigue, decreased appetite, diarrhea, peripheral sensory neuropathy, abdominal pain, constipation, decreased weight, hypersensitivity reactions, and pyrexia.
Patients who received zolbetuximab.clzb in SPOTLIGHT and GLOW experienced more nausea (76%) and vomiting (67%) compared with patients who received placebo (56% nausea and 33% vomiting).
In SPOTLIGHT, serious adverse reactions occurred in 45% of patients treated with zolbetuximab.clzb in combination with mFOLFOX6
Permanent discontinuation of VYLOY due to an adverse reaction occurred in 20% of patients; the most common adverse reactions leading to discontinuation (\ge2%) were nausea and vomiting.
